primary_source: Yale Bulletin, David Geffen School of Drama 2026-2027 (Series 122 No. 14, 30 Aug 2026), https://bulletin.yale.edu/sites/default/files/david-geffen-school-of-drama-2026-2027.pdf - downloaded and text-extracted; page refs are the Bulletin's printed pages

claims.claim: Every figure is the school's own for 2026-2027, read from the Bulletin published 30 August 2026
claims.source: Bulletin 2026-27 cover
claims.note: The Bulletin is dated August 30, 2026. But several figures below are SLATE's and are not all labelled, so 'every figure' overclaims.
claims.label: Simplified

claims.claim: Class size: 16 actors admitted each year
claims.source: https://www.drama.yale.edu/training/acting/application-requirements/frequently-asked-questions/
claims.note: The FAQ says 'The acting program admits 15-17 people each year.' 16 is the middle of the range, not a fixed size.
claims.label: Simplified

claims.claim: Six terms, which is also the length of the degree
claims.source: Bulletin pp.21, 182, 191 (three years in residence; tuition scholarship 'ordinarily limited to six terms'; six semesters as the normal time frame)
claims.note: The MFA must be finished within nine semesters, and the faculty may cut residency to two years in rare cases.
claims.label: Documented

claims.claim: Dean Evan Yionoulis, Dean and Artistic Director of Yale Rep, since 2026-07-01
claims.source: https://news.yale.edu/2026/04/07/yionoulis-named-next-dean-david-geffen-school-drama-yale; Bulletin p.9
claims.note: Her full title is Elizabeth Parker Ware Dean, effective July 1, 2026.
claims.label: Documented

claims.claim: Chair of Acting: Tamilla Woodard
claims.source: Bulletin p.9 and p.23; https://www.drama.yale.edu/training/acting
claims.note: Grace Zandarski is Associate Chair.
claims.label: Documented

claims.claim: Minimum age 21: the MFA asks for a bachelor's degree
claims.source: Bulletin p.21 (Certificate in Drama); drama.yale.edu Acting FAQ
claims.note: The Acting program also admits people without a bachelor's degree, who earn the Certificate in Drama and must have been out of high school for at least five years. An MFA admit with an early degree could be under 21. The code calls this SLATE's reading but ignores the Certificate route.
claims.label: Original SLATE content

claims.claim: Tuition $40,750, covered for every student by the David Geffen gift
claims.source: Bulletin p.182: 'tuition fee ... $40,750 ... 100 percent tuition support, in perpetuity' ($150M gift, 2021)
claims.note: Covers full-time degree and certificate students.
claims.label: Documented

claims.claim: Living expenses $28,028, including the Yale Health Hospitalization/Specialty plan, which is billed
claims.source: Bulletin pp.182, 187 (living-expense table)
claims.note: The coverage can be waived with proof of other insurance, and it runs for 12 months.
claims.label: Documented

claims.claim: Yale Health plan $3,764
claims.source: Bulletin p.187 table ('Yale Health Hospitalization/Specialty Coverage $3,764', nine months)
claims.label: Documented

claims.claim: Books and supplies $913 to $2,373 by program; the actor's figure isn't published, so SLATE uses $2,373
claims.source: Bulletin p.182
claims.note: The range is documented. The choice of the maximum is labelled as SLATE's.
claims.label: Documented

claims.claim: Aid for living costs is need-based and assesses the family; where there is need, a living-expense scholarship meets it and the rest is paid to the bank
claims.source: Bulletin pp.187-189; https://www.drama.yale.edu/admissions/financial-aid/
claims.note: Need-based aid that assesses parents is documented. But the scholarship is awarded only after the student contribution, parental contribution, a first-year loan and work-study are counted. The financial-aid page says 'most first year students borrow $9,500.' Even high-need students average 95% of cost covered over three years, not the full need. The code leaves out the loan and the student contribution.
claims.label: Simplified

claims.claim: The living-expense scholarship is paid in two instalments, at the start of the fall and spring terms
claims.source: Bulletin p.188; drama.yale.edu financial aid ('half in the fall term and the balance in the spring term')

claims.source: https://college.yale.edu/academics/academic-calendar/future-and-future-provisional-academic-calendars ('2029: Commencement M 5/21'); https://commencement.yale.edu (Monday before Memorial Day)

claims.claim: Required course codes, titles and teachers for 2026-27 (35 courses, DRAM 103a/b to DRAM 793b)
claims.source: Bulletin pp.24-34 (Plan of Study and Courses of Instruction)
claims.note: Every listed code, title and teacher matches. Exceptions: (a) DRAM 273b has no description in the Bulletin and no named teacher, so 'Acting faculty' is SLATE's placeholder. (b) The Bulletin describes DRAM 303a/b as two semesters but the plan of study lists DRAM 303a; the code follows the plan. (c) DRAM 873a/b is taught by 'Paul Walsh and Faculty' (Walsh is emeritus). (d) Chris Bayes (DRAM 263) is on leave in fall 2026. (e) The code leaves out required courses DRAM 4b (Critical Response Process), 53a, 180a, 533a/b (all three years), 563a and 863b (Anti-Racist Theater, required for graduation), yet calls the list 'A required course'.
claims.label: Simplified

claims.claim: The Bulletin restricts outside work only while classes are in session, so the summer is the student's own
claims.source: Bulletin p.148 ('discourages students from pursuing outside ... work while school is in session')

claims.claim: At the end of each term the faculty weigh attendance and growth: good standing, notice of academic concern, academic warning, dismissal with no readmission, 'as the Bulletin sets it out'
claims.note: The four stages and no readmission are documented. But the Bulletin says the faculty evaluate 'regularly' and may act 'at any time'. A concern escalates if not fixed 'within one semester', and a warning carries its own deadline. A student may also be dismissed without a prior warning. The automatic one-step-per-term ladder and the attendance-and-growth test are SLATE's design.
claims.label: Simplified
